VEGANScreener + metabolomics

Q2: Associations between VS_total and the metabolome in vegans.

This script explores patterns in the metabolome profiles of vegans, particularly by linking them to the VEGANScreener score (VS_total).

The script is divided into two parts, based on how the metabolome datasets were integrated (see the preprocessing scripts for details). The first part analyzes the sPCA dataset, which is used for multivariate analysis, PCA visualization, PERMANOVA, and the machine-learning models. The second part uses the concatenated dataset (LC-MS and NMR combined) for the univariate analysis.

The analysis is composed of the following main parts:

  1. Global visualization — the first three components, color-coded by VS_total.

  2. PERMANOVA — how much of the variation can be explained by various external variables: dist(Metabolome) ~ sex + bmi + age + veganDuration + country*VS_total

  3. Univariate analysis (feature-wise model) — linear modelling of each metabolite against various external variables: Metabolite ~ sex + bmi + age + veganDuration + Country*VS_total

  4. Random forest (RF) classification — the model is trained and validated by bootstrapping with 500 iterations, and used to distinguish between participants in the 1st and 3rd tertiles of VS_total. Two types of models are trained:

  1. a model on the original sPCA dataset
  2. a model on the sPCA dataset after regressing out the covariates.

1 Import

metadata_df <- read.table(
  file =  "../../data/preprocessed/metadata_preprocessed_v3.tsv",
  header = TRUE)  

lcms_df <- read.table(
  file= "../../data/preprocessed/metabolomics/lc_ms_preprocessed_INT_v3.tsv",
  check.names = FALSE)

nmr_df <- read.table(
  file = "../../data/preprocessed/metabolomics/nmr_preprocessed_INT_v3.tsv",
  check.names = FALSE)

spca_integrated_df <-  read.table(
  file = "../../data/preprocessed/metabolomics/spca_integrated_vegans_INT_v3.tsv",
  check.names = FALSE)

Scaling — when metadata columns are used as covariates, they need to be scaled so that each has a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1.

metadata_scaled_df <- metadata_df
metadata_scaled_df[,-c(1,3,5,6,8)] <- apply(metadata_df[,-c(1,3,5,6,8)],2,scale)
metadata_scaled_df <- metadata_scaled_df %>%
  mutate(sex=as.factor(sex),
         country=as.factor(country),
         group=as.factor(group),
         diet_supplements=as.factor(diet_supplements))

3 SPCA

The sPCA dataset was created by concatenating the LC-MS and NMR datasets and applying the mixOmics::spca() function. See the preprocessing script for details.

mixOmics::spca() performs sparse Principal Component Analysis (sPCA), which works like regular PCA but adds a sparsity constraint so that only a subset of variables contributes to each component. The degree of sparsity is controlled by a penalization term, which makes the components easier to interpret because irrelevant or noisy variables are given loadings of zero.

3.2 PERMANOVA

The test shows how much of the variation in the metabolome is explained by sex, age, BMI, vegan duration, country, and VS_total.

Variables were added sequentially (Type I sums of squares), so each p-value and R² reflects a partial effect after adjusting for the variables above it. The model first accounts for variation due to sex, age, vegan diet duration, BMI, and country of origin. It then accounts for the main effect of VS_total, and finally tests whether the effect of VS_total varies by country of origin (the interaction term).

VS_total explains 2.588% of the variation after adjusting for sex, age, BMI, country, and diet duration. This result is statistically significant (p<0.001).

However, country of origin still explains the largest share of the variation, around 10%. The interaction effect is not significant, suggesting that the effect of VS_total is consistent across countries.

# Create Euclidean distance matrix
dist_mat <- vegdist(spca_integrated_df, 
                    method = "euclidean")

# Test whether vegan vs omnivore differ in metabolomics
adonis_result <- adonis2(
  dist_mat ~ sex + bmi + age + vegan_duration + country*VS_total,
  data = metadata_scaled_df , 
  permutations = 999,
  by="terms")

print(adonis_result)

3.3 RF model

3.3.1 Original model

sub_metadata_df <- metadata_df %>%
dplyr::filter(
  tertile_label %in% c("1st_VStertile","3rd_VStertile"))

sub_spca_integrated_df <- spca_integrated_df[as.character(sub_metadata_df$study_id),]
model_name <- "VS_tertile_vegan" 

prepared_df <- model_preparation(sub_spca_integrated_df,
                                 sub_metadata_df,
                                 predicting_col = "tertile_label")

rf_model <- make_rf_model(data=prepared_df,
                            outcome="Group",
                            N = 500,
                           file = model_name,
                            reuse=TRUE)

roc_c <- roc_curve(model_object = rf_model, 
                   group = c("low VS_total","high VS_total"),CI = TRUE) 

roc_c <- ggtheme(roc_c) + 
  theme(legend.position="none",title = element_text(size=8))

roc_c

3.4 RF importance

3.4.1 Original model

PC5 and PC10 are the most important variables for the RF model.

load("../intermediate_files/models/VS_tertile_vegan/rf_model.RData")

  rownames_to_column("PC") %>%
  `colnames<-`(c("PC","Importance")) 

var_imp <- var_imp %>% dplyr::mutate(PC=factor(PC,levels = PC[order(var_imp$Importance,decreasing = TRUE)])) 

ggplot(var_imp) + 
  geom_col(aes(x=PC,y=Importance))

4.2 Univariate analysis

We test the differences between diets and VS_total using a generalized linear model, while adjusting for covariates.

4.2.1 Metabolite-wise model

4.2.1.1 Continuous analysis

A GLM is used to identify which metabolites are significantly related to the VS score, adjusting for age, sex, country, and dietary group:

Metabolite ~ sex + bmi + age + eq_vegan_dur_total + Country*VS_total

results_list <- lapply(colnames(concat_integrated_df), 
                       function(x) fit_glm(x,concat_for_uni,
                                           tested_variable = "VS_total"))
results_df <- do.call(rbind, results_list)

results_df$p_adjusted <- p.adjust(results_df$Pr...t..,method = "BH")

Significant results — 9 metabolites:

Dispersion

dispersion <- vs_effects %>%
  group_by(metabolite) %>%
  summarise(
    range      = max(emmean) - min(emmean),      # simplest: spread between highest and lowest 
    sd         = sd(emmean),                      # standard deviation of the 5 country means
    cv         = sd(emmean) / abs(mean(emmean)),  # coefficient of variation (relative dispersion)
    min_mean   = min(emmean),
    max_mean   = max(emmean),
    min_VS = tertile_label[which.min(emmean)],
    max_VS = tertile_label[which.max(emmean)]
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(range))

4.2.2.2 Network construction

Edge list

edges <- vs_effects %>%
  filter(p_adj < 0.05) %>%
  #filter(abs(emmean)>0.3) %>%
  dplyr::select(from = tertile_label, to = metabolite, 
         emmean = emmean) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(from=as.character(from),
         weight=abs(emmean))

edges$from <- as.character(edges$from)
edges$to   <- as.character(edges$to)

Nodes table

tertiles <- as.character(unique(edges$from))
metabs <- as.character(unique(edges$to))

nodes <- data.frame(
  name = c(tertiles, metabs),
  type = c(rep(TRUE, length(tertiles)), rep(FALSE, length(metabs))) # TRUE = tertile, FALSE = metabolite
)

Build igraph object

g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = edges, vertices = nodes, directed = FALSE)

Visualize

VS_colors <- c("1st_VStertile"="#D73027",
               "2nd_VStertile"="orange",
               "3rd_VStertile"="#1A9850")

# Assign colors to nodes: countries get their color, metabolites gray
V(g)$color <- ifelse(V(g)$type,
                     VS_colors[V(g)$name],
                     "gray70")

set.seed(123)
ggraph(g, layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(aes(width = abs(weight), color = emmean > 0), alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_edge_color_manual(values = c("lightblue", "lightpink"), labels = c("<0", ">0")) +
  geom_node_point(aes(shape=type,color = name), size = 6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = setNames(V(g)$color, V(g)$name)) +  # node colors
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +
  theme_void() +
  guides(color = "none")

6 Metabolite-based veganscreener score

6.1 Continuous univariate test

To build a vegan index from the concatenated dataset, we use linear regression to obtain coefficients for the significant variables identified across the analysis:

sign <- final_significance
sign
[1] "PA.44.5."           "PC.34.1."           "PC.40.6."          
[4] "SM.d42.2."          "LysoPC.22.6."       "Indoleacrylic.acid"
[7] "LysoPC.17.0."       "Ergothionenine"     "Acetylornithin"    
# define the variables
plot_list <- list()
rhos <- rep(NA,5)
ps <- rep(NA,5)

# split the datasets for cross-validation
concat_for_index <- concat_for_uni[sample(rownames(concat_for_uni)),]
cv_splits <- cv_folds(concat_for_index,folds = 5)

final_df_veganindex <- data.frame()

# cross validation loop
vars_selection <- list()
for (i in 1:length(cv_splits)){
  unisub_df <- concat_for_uni[cv_splits[[i]]$train,]
  results_list <- lapply(colnames(concat_integrated_df), 
                       function(x) fit_glm(x,unisub_df,
                                           tested_variable = "VS_total"))
  results_df <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
  
  results_df$p_adjusted <- p.adjust(results_df$Pr...t..,method = "BH")

  vars <- results_df$metabolite[results_df$p_adjusted<0.05 & results_df$variable=="VS_total"]
  vars_selection[[i]] <- vars
  
  # Wrap all variable names in backticks
  vars_safe <- paste0("`", vars, "`")
  
  fml <- as.formula(paste("VS_total ~", paste(vars_safe, collapse = " + ")))
  
  # fit the model
  model <- lm(fml, unisub_df)
  
  # predict the result on validation dataset
  VG_index <- stats::predict(model,concat_for_uni[cv_splits[[i]]$val,])
  
  # store the predicted index
  sub_df <- concat_for_uni[cv_splits[[i]]$val,]
  sub_df$VGindex <- VG_index
  final_df_veganindex <- rbind(final_df_veganindex,sub_df)
  
  # calculate correlation 
  cor_test <- cor.test(sub_df$VGindex,
               sub_df$VS_total,
               method = "spearman")
  cor_val <- cor_test$estimate
  if (cor_test$p.value >0.05) cor_val = 0

  # plot the result
  p <- ggplot(sub_df,

subtitle: "Q2: Associations between VS_total and the metabolome in vegans."

  html:  
    embed-resources: true
    keep-md: false
    toc: true
    toc-expand: 3
    toc-depth: 6
    toc-location: left

    number-depth: 6

      body-width: 1000px

**This script explores patterns in the metabolome profiles of vegans, particularly by linking them to the VEGANScreener score (VS_total).**


The script is divided into two parts, based on how the metabolome datasets were integrated (see the preprocessing scripts for details). The first part analyzes the **sPCA dataset**, which is used for multivariate analysis, PCA visualization, PERMANOVA, and the machine-learning models. The second part uses the **concatenated dataset** (LC-MS and NMR combined) for the univariate analysis. 

The analysis is composed of the following main parts:

1.  Global visualization — the first three components, color-coded by **VS_total**.

2.  PERMANOVA — how much of the variation can be explained by various external variables:
  dist(Metabolome) \~ sex + bmi + age + veganDuration + country***VS_total**

3.  Univariate analysis (feature-wise model) — linear modelling of each metabolite against various external variables:
  Metabolite \~  sex + bmi + age + veganDuration + Country***VS_total**
  
4.  Random forest (RF) classification — the model is trained and validated by bootstrapping with 500 iterations, and used to distinguish between participants in the **1st and 3rd tertiles of VS_total**. Two types of models are trained:
a) a model on the original sPCA dataset
b) a model on the sPCA dataset after regressing out the covariates.

```{r,echo=FALSE}
source("custom_functions_vegans.R")
```

# SPCA

The sPCA dataset was created by concatenating the LC-MS and NMR datasets and applying the mixOmics::spca() function. See the preprocessing script for details. 

mixOmics::spca() performs **sparse Principal Component Analysis (sPCA)**, which works like regular PCA but adds a sparsity constraint so that only a subset of variables contributes to each component.
The degree of sparsity is controlled by a penalization term, which makes the components easier to interpret because irrelevant or noisy variables are given loadings of zero.

## PERMANOVA

The test shows how much of the variation in the metabolome is explained by sex, age, BMI, vegan duration, country, and **VS_total**.

Variables were added sequentially (Type I sums of squares), so each p-value and R² reflects a partial effect after adjusting for the variables above it. The model first accounts for variation due to sex, age, vegan diet duration, BMI, and country of origin. It then accounts for the main effect of VS_total, and finally tests whether the effect of VS_total varies by country of origin (the interaction term).

----------------------

VS_total explains **2.588%** of the variation after adjusting for sex, age, BMI, country, and diet duration. This result is statistically significant (p<0.001).

However, country of origin still explains the largest share of the variation, around **10%**. The interaction effect is not significant, suggesting that the effect of VS_total is consistent across countries.

```{r}
# Create Euclidean distance matrix
dist_mat <- vegdist(spca_integrated_df, 
                    method = "euclidean")

# Test whether vegan vs omnivore differ in metabolomics
adonis_result <- adonis2(
  dist_mat ~ sex + bmi + age + vegan_duration + country*VS_total,
  data = metadata_scaled_df , 
  permutations = 999,
  by="terms")

print(adonis_result)
```

```{r,fig.width=6,fig.height=2}
adonis_result <- adonis_result[-c(7,9),] %>% rownames_to_column("Var")
adonis_result$Var <- factor(adonis_result$Var,levels = rev(c("sex","bmi","age", "vegan_duration","country","VS_total", "Residual")))
p <- ggplot(adonis_result, aes(fill=Var, x=R2, y="Metabolome")) + 
    geom_bar(position="stack", stat="identity") + 
  ylab("") + xlab("Partial variance explained (R²)") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values=rev(c("#ffffcc","#b3cde3","#ccebc5",
                                 "#decbe4","#fed9a6","darkred",
                                 "lightgrey")),name = "Covariate")  

p <- ggtheme(p)

p

p_pca[[2]] <- p
p_pca[[3]] <- adonis_result
```

```{r,fig.height=5,fig.width=5}
model_name <- "VS_tertile_vegan"
```

## RF importance

### Original model

**PC5** and **PC10** are the most important variables for the RF model.

```{r,fig.width=10}
load("../intermediate_files/models/VS_tertile_vegan/rf_model.RData")

var_imp <- as.data.frame(importance(rf_model$trained_model)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("PC") %>%
  `colnames<-`(c("PC","Importance")) 

var_imp <- var_imp %>% dplyr::mutate(PC=factor(PC,levels = PC[order(var_imp$Importance,decreasing = TRUE)])) 

ggplot(var_imp) + 
  geom_col(aes(x=PC,y=Importance))
```

### Adjusted model

As above, **PC5** is the most important variable, with a marked drop in importance for the PCs after it. 

```{r,fig.width=10}
load("../intermediate_files/models/adjusted_vstotal_model_vegan/rf_model.RData")

var_imp <- as.data.frame(importance(rf_model$trained_model)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("PC") %>%
  `colnames<-`(c("PC","Importance")) 

var_imp <- var_imp %>% dplyr::mutate(PC=factor(PC,levels = PC[order(var_imp$Importance,decreasing = TRUE)])) 

ggplot(var_imp) + 
  geom_col(aes(x=PC,y=Importance))
```

### Visualization

## Univariate analysis

We test the differences between diets and VS_total using a generalized linear model, while adjusting for covariates.

### Metabolite-wise model

#### Continuous analysis

A GLM is used to identify which metabolites are significantly related to the VS score, adjusting for age, sex, country, and dietary group:

Metabolite ~ sex + bmi + age + eq_vegan_dur_total + Country*VS_total

```{r}
results_list <- lapply(colnames(concat_integrated_df), 
                       function(x) fit_glm(x,concat_for_uni,
                                           tested_variable = "VS_total"))
results_df <- do.call(rbind, results_list)

results_df$p_adjusted <- p.adjust(results_df$Pr...t..,method = "BH")
```

```{r}
dispersion <- vs_effects %>%
  group_by(metabolite) %>%
  summarise(
    range      = max(emmean) - min(emmean),      # simplest: spread between highest and lowest 
    sd         = sd(emmean),                      # standard deviation of the 5 country means
    cv         = sd(emmean) / abs(mean(emmean)),  # coefficient of variation (relative dispersion)
    min_mean   = min(emmean),
    max_mean   = max(emmean),
    min_VS = tertile_label[which.min(emmean)],
    max_VS = tertile_label[which.max(emmean)]
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(range))
```

Network construction:

#### Network construction

**Edge list**

```{r}
edges <- vs_effects %>%
  filter(p_adj < 0.05) %>%
  #filter(abs(emmean)>0.3) %>%
  dplyr::select(from = tertile_label, to = metabolite, 
         emmean = emmean) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(from=as.character(from),
         weight=abs(emmean))

edges$from <- as.character(edges$from)
edges$to   <- as.character(edges$to)
```

**Nodes table**

```{r}
tertiles <- as.character(unique(edges$from))
metabs <- as.character(unique(edges$to))

nodes <- data.frame(
  name = c(tertiles, metabs),
  type = c(rep(TRUE, length(tertiles)), rep(FALSE, length(metabs))) # TRUE = tertile, FALSE = metabolite
)
```

**Build igraph object**

```{r}
g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = edges, vertices = nodes, directed = FALSE)
```

**Visualize**

```{r,fig.height=6,fig.width=6}
VS_colors <- c("1st_VStertile"="#D73027",
               "2nd_VStertile"="orange",
               "3rd_VStertile"="#1A9850")

# Assign colors to nodes: countries get their color, metabolites gray
V(g)$color <- ifelse(V(g)$type,
                     VS_colors[V(g)$name],
                     "gray70")

set.seed(123)
ggraph(g, layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(aes(width = abs(weight), color = emmean > 0), alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_edge_color_manual(values = c("lightblue", "lightpink"), labels = c("<0", ">0")) +
  geom_node_point(aes(shape=type,color = name), size = 6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = setNames(V(g)$color, V(g)$name)) +  # node colors
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +
  theme_void() +
  guides(color = "none")

```

#### Degree calculation


```{r}
# Calculate degree
deg <- degree(g, mode = "all")

# Add to node dataframe
node_degree_df <- data.frame(
  name = names(deg),
  degree = deg,
  type = V(g)$type
)

# Separate interpretation
vs_nodes <- node_degree_df %>% dplyr::filter(type == TRUE)
metabolite_nodes <- node_degree_df %>% dplyr::filter(type == FALSE)

vs_nodes %>% arrange(desc(degree))
metabolite_nodes %>% arrange(desc(degree))
```

**Weighted degree**
- reflects the cumulative magnitude of associations, not just the number of links.

```{r}
strength_vals <- strength(g, weights = E(g)$weight)

node_strength_df <- data.frame(
  name = names(strength_vals),
  strength = strength_vals,
  type = V(g)$type
)

# Separate interpretation
vs_nodes <- node_strength_df %>% dplyr::filter(type == TRUE)
metabolite_nodes <- node_strength_df %>% dplyr::filter(type == FALSE)

vs_nodes %>% arrange(desc(strength))
metabolite_nodes %>% arrange(desc(strength))
```

# Metabolite-based veganscreener score

## Continuous univariate test

To build a vegan index from the concatenated dataset, we use linear regression to obtain coefficients for the significant variables identified across the analysis:

```{r}
sign <- final_significance
sign
```



```{r}
# define the variables
plot_list <- list()
rhos <- rep(NA,5)
ps <- rep(NA,5)

# split the datasets for cross-validation
concat_for_index <- concat_for_uni[sample(rownames(concat_for_uni)),]
cv_splits <- cv_folds(concat_for_index,folds = 5)

final_df_veganindex <- data.frame()

# cross validation loop
vars_selection <- list()
for (i in 1:length(cv_splits)){
  unisub_df <- concat_for_uni[cv_splits[[i]]$train,]
  results_list <- lapply(colnames(concat_integrated_df), 
                       function(x) fit_glm(x,unisub_df,
                                           tested_variable = "VS_total"))
  results_df <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
  
  results_df$p_adjusted <- p.adjust(results_df$Pr...t..,method = "BH")

  vars <- results_df$metabolite[results_df$p_adjusted<0.05 & results_df$variable=="VS_total"]
  vars_selection[[i]] <- vars
  
  # Wrap all variable names in backticks
  vars_safe <- paste0("`", vars, "`")
  
  fml <- as.formula(paste("VS_total ~", paste(vars_safe, collapse = " + ")))
  
  # fit the model
  model <- lm(fml, unisub_df)
  
  # predict the result on validation dataset
  VG_index <- stats::predict(model,concat_for_uni[cv_splits[[i]]$val,])
  
  # store the predicted index
  sub_df <- concat_for_uni[cv_splits[[i]]$val,]
  sub_df$VGindex <- VG_index
  final_df_veganindex <- rbind(final_df_veganindex,sub_df)
  
  # calculate correlation 
  cor_test <- cor.test(sub_df$VGindex,
               sub_df$VS_total,
               method = "spearman")
  cor_val <- cor_test$estimate
  if (cor_test$p.value >0.05) cor_val = 0

  # plot the result
  p <- ggplot(sub_df, 
              aes_string(x = "VGindex", y = "VS_total"),
              color="blue") +
       geom_point() + 
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") + 
    theme_minimal() + 
    ggtitle(paste("Rho =",round(cor_val,2)))

  plot_list[[i]] <- p
  rhos[i] <- round(cor_val,2)
  ps[i] <- cor_test$p.value
}

```

```{r}
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold",size = 9),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right") + 
  labs(fill = "Median metabolite z-score") +
  xlab("Vegans (ordered and grouped by VEGANScreener score)") + 
  ylab("") + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "darkcyan", mid = "white", high = "brown", midpoint = 0)

# get legend
leg_heat_p <- ggpubr::get_legend(p_heat)

# remove legend
p_heat <- p_heat + theme(legend.position = "right")
```


```{r}
annotation_df <- concat_significant_df
annotation_df$metabolite <- factor(annotation_df$metabolite,
                                   levels=annotation_df$metabolite)


ann_p <- ggplot(
  data=annotation_df,
  aes(x = "Estimate", y = metabolite, fill = Estimate)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#313695", mid = "white", high = "#A50026", midpoint = 0) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y= element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right") + 
  ylab("Significant metabolites") + 
  xlab("") + 
  labs(fill="LM estimate")

ann_p <- fix_labels(ann_p)

# get legend
leg_ann_p <- ggpubr::get_legend(ann_p)

# Remove legend from the original plot
ann_p <-ann_p + theme(legend.position = "right")

```

```{r}
# correlations
df_for_plot <- concat_integrated_df %>% dplyr::select(final_significance)
df_for_plot <- df_for_plot[,concat_significant_df$metabolite]
corr_object <- cor(concat_for_uni$VS_total,df_for_plot,method="spearman")
corr_df <- data.frame(Metabolite=colnames(corr_object),
                      Rho=corr_object[1,])
corr_df$Metabolite <- factor(corr_df$Metabolite,
                             levels=corr_df$Metabolite)

p_corr <- ggplot(corr_df) + 
  geom_point(aes(x="Rho",y= Metabolite,size = abs(Rho), fill = Rho, color=Rho), 
             shape = 21) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(name = "Rho", 
                       low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
    scale_color_gradient2(name = "Rho", 
                          low = "blue", mid = "white", 
                          high = "red", midpoint = 0) + 
  guides(size = "none") + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y= element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right") + 
  xlab("") 


leg_corr_p <- ggpubr::get_legend(p_corr)

# Remove legend from the original plot
p_corr <-
  p_corr +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right")
```

```{r}
legends <- ggarrange(leg_heat_p, leg_ann_p, leg_corr_p,nrow = 3, align = "hv")

p <- wrap_plots(ann_p,p_corr,p_heat,legends,ncol=4,widths = c(0.1,0.15, 1, 1))
```


```{r}
cbar <- guide_colourbar(barheight = unit(1.8, "cm"),
                        barwidth  = unit(0.35, "cm"),
                        title.position = "top")

p_heat <- p_heat + guides(fill   = cbar)   # z-score (fill)
ann_p  <- ann_p  + guides(fill   = cbar)   # LM estimate (fill)
p_corr <- p_corr + guides(fill = cbar)   # Rho (colour, not fill)

p <- wrap_plots(ann_p, p_corr, p_heat, ncol = 3, widths = c(0.1, 0.15, 1)) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position  = "right",
        legend.box       = "vertical",
        legend.title     = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
        legend.text      = element_text(size = 8))
```
